title: Pricing vs SLA: Headcount & Cost Flex Grid (Dec 2026)
summary: Working worksheet to evaluate how different per-token pricing bands and SLA targets map to required headcount, monthly unit cost, and gross margin under three capacity cases. This is intentionally tactical: used to brief GTM and Eng leads on trade-offs for a potential SLA-based price ladder and to quantify hiring/infra levers required to keep margins above target.
scenarios: Base (moderate growth): volume growth = 15% YoY, steady latency targets (p95 < 250ms for standard tier).
High-growth (scale): volume growth = 60% YoY, opt-in burst capacity and higher dedicated infra required to meet p95 < 200ms for premium customers.
Downturn / Price pressure: price elasticity triggers -20% realized price, volume flat to -5%; conservative hiring and delayed hire freezes.
assumptions: Token volume baseline: 2.4 billion input+output tokens / month (2,400,000k tokens).
Prices evaluated are per 1k tokens (units). Base price = $0.80 / 1k tokens for hosted API standard tier.
Infra OPEX baseline: $0.22 / 1k tokens (includes GPU amortization, cloud egress, storage, network).
Staff fully-loaded cost allocation to inference ops: $0.18 / 1k tokens at current scale (includes eng infra, SRE, infra ops, and monitoring amortized).
Desired minimum gross margin target = 45% after infra+staff variable costs (not including sales/marketing).
SLA premium multiplier: premium tier (p95 < 200ms) requires ~1.6x infra & 1.25x staff allocation vs standard tier.

Notes: revenue = price_per_1k * token_k_units; infra_cost_monthly = infra OPEX per 1k * token_k_units (0.22 * 2,400,000 = $528k). staff_cost_monthly uses Base staff allocation. Gross margin = (revenue - infra - staff) / revenue.
sla_premium_impact: Premium SLA (p95 < 200ms) assumptions: infra OPEX multiplier = 1.6x, staff allocation multiplier = 1.25x.
Under Base price ($0.80) premium SLA monthly numbers: revenue (same volume) = $1.92M, infra = $844.8k, staff = $343.8k → margin ≈ 27.8%.
To maintain 45% margin at premium SLA with current volume, price needs to increase to ≈ $1.22 / 1k (+52.5%).

Alternatively, margin can be preserved by a combination of 1) infra optimizations (~25% reduction via quantization/packing), 2) targeted automation saving ~10% of staff allocation, and 3) exploring committed reserved capacity discounts reducing infra by 15%.
break_even_headcount_analysis: If price is set to $0.72 / 1k (-10%), with Base infra, to reach 45% margin we must reduce staff allocation to ~$0.09 / 1k (from $0.18) or increase price or reduce infra by ~35%.

High-growth case: adding premium customers expands revenue but increases infra & staff; at +10% price we approach 45% margin only if infra efficiency gains of at least 18% are realized within 6 months or if we shift 30% of traffic to cached/replicated zero-cost paths (prefix caching).
key_tradeoffs: Aggressive SLA promises (lower latency / stricter p95) increase unit cost materially — either require higher price or significantly more infra/staff investment.
Price cuts to win market share must be paired with a clear infra optimization roadmap; otherwise margins erode quickly and hiring plans need to be frozen.
Reserved capacity commits (Dedicated contracts) can reduce infra OPEX per token, but increase capital commitment and reduce flexibility for model changes (quantization/architecture shifts).
Customer segmentation (standard vs premium) allows price differentiation but adds product complexity and requires sales enablement to sell SLA uplift.
recommended_actions: Run a short 8-week infra optimization sprint (quantization + kernel tuning + caching) with goal: 20–25% reduction in infra OPEX / 1k tokens. (Owner: serving-runtime lead)
Model a price ladder for standard / premium with experimental rollout: +10% price for premium with a 30-day canary and telemetry to track churn/hard-elasticity (Owner: finance + product).
Delay non-critical headcount hires for 2 quarters in the Downturn scenario simulation; prioritize automation hires that reduce staff allocation per token. (Owner: People Ops + Eng Leads).
Negotiate pilot reserved capacity discounts with two cloud partners to validate 12–18% unit cost reduction at 6–12 month commit levels. (Owner: infra procurement).
Share this sheet and a one-pager with GTM leadership and schedule a cross-functional review (finance, eng, product, sales) to finalize price ladder by Jan 20, 2027.
